Maki $label is a release candidate, built by the release workflow from
commit [`$commit`](https://github.com/$repository/commit/$commit).

**This is a pre-release and is not production-qualified.** Production
approval is pending and no configuration of Maki is production-qualified; see
the [project status](https://github.com/$repository/blob/$tag/docs/status.md)
and the [support matrix](https://github.com/$repository/blob/$tag/docs/deployment/support-matrix.md).
Use it on disposable hosts.

## Assets

| Asset | What it is |
|---|---|
| `$deb` | Debian package for $deb_platform; package version `$version` |
| `$rpm` | RPM package for $rpm_platform; package version `$version-$rpm_release` |
| `$source` | The exact committed source of `$commit` (including `Cargo.lock`) that both packages were built from |
| `$deb_manifest` | Build record of the Debian package: commit, build distribution, toolchain, build command, dependencies and hashes |
| `$rpm_manifest` | Build record of the RPM: commit, build distribution, toolchain, requirements and hash |
| `SHA256SUMS` | SHA-256 of every asset above |

Both packages carry the candidate version `$version`
([version policy](https://github.com/$repository/blob/$tag/docs/releasing.md#candidate-version-ordering)).
The asset names use the tag instead, because GitHub rewrites `~` and `+` in
asset names. The manifests record the names the build gave the files. The
"Source code" archives that GitHub attaches to every release are generated by
GitHub from the tag; they are not part of `SHA256SUMS`.

## Integrity

The assets are **not signed**, and there is no build attestation. Their
integrity rests on `SHA256SUMS` alone, which is published beside them and so
does not prove who published them. Download `SHA256SUMS` and the assets you
need into one directory, then check them:

```bash
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
```

## Install

- Debian 12: follow the
  [Debian installation guide](https://github.com/$repository/blob/$tag/docs/getting-started/installation-debian.md)
  from "Install the Maki package", with `apt install ./$deb`.
- RHEL 9 and its rebuilds (not qualified): follow the
  [RHEL 9 installation guide](https://github.com/$repository/blob/$tag/docs/getting-started/installation-rhel.md)
  from "Install the Maki package", with `dnf install ./$rpm`.
